On 1000 expert-labelled PubMedQA questions (EvalKit run `r-f0f3b432a413`, judges: dual, calibration: uncalibrated); 95% intervals in square brackets:

| Model | Accuracy | Correct and grounded (claude-opus-5-5) | Correct and grounded (gpt-6.1-sol) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-e2b-base-q4 | 0.501 [0.469, 0.532] | 0.418 [0.387, 0.448] | 0.394 [0.364, 0.424] |
| **gemma-e2b-grounded-q4** | 0.728 [0.700, 0.755] | 0.388 [0.358, 0.419] | 0.330 [0.301, 0.359] |
| claude-haiku-5-5 | 0.685 [0.656, 0.714] | 0.345 [0.316, 0.374] | 0.231 [0.205, 0.257] |
| gpt-6-luna | 0.579 [0.548, 0.611] | 0.431 [0.401, 0.462] | 0.290 [0.262, 0.319] |

Caveats: judge not calibrated for this task (see docs/calibrate-your-task.md); claude-opus-5-5: never stamped calibrated: the reference labels are its own model's (Claude Opus 5.5), so its held-out kappa 0.397 [0.263, 0.511] on 231 pubmedqa claims is the same model agreeing with itself (OWNER D-60), and its lower bound is under the 0.4 bar; reported only, its numbers stay published; gpt-6.1-sol: calibrated, held-out kappa 0.598 [0.468, 0.711] on 231 pubmedqa claims, lower bound at least 0.4 (OWNER D-59): agreement with a Claude Opus 5.5 reference labeller (a model's labels, not a human expert's; OWNER D-60). Gemma-family check (40 claims from main_v2): agreement 0.950, kappa 0.893 [0.722, 1.000]. The local demo serves the benchmarked Q4_K_M GGUF (OWNER D-63); the published bf16 weights agree with it on the label for 0.956 of 500 dev prompts. On a laptop (Apple M3 Max) the Q4_K_M GGUF generates 105.1 tokens/s (p50). Research only, not medical advice.
